title: How Transformers Finally Ate Vision – Isaac Robinson, Roboflow
talk_summary: A history of vision architectures arguing that plain ViTs won because massive ViT-specific pretraining (MAE, DINO) plus LLM-derived speedups (FlashAttention) outweighed hand-built inductive biases, and that deployment flexibility now comes from pretraining-compatible neural architecture search. It is a computer-vision research retrospective with no agent-orchestration content.

takeaways.technique: Pretraining-compatible architecture search instead of one-size-fits-all model
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep one foundation backbone and expose flexible knobs (depth/width/resolution) chosen per target data and hardware, generating a family of models via NAS rather than retraining a fixed giant model per deployment.
takeaways.numbers: ~40x speedup for same accuracy vs fine-tuning SAM 3; 15x for meaningful improvement; SAM 3 is 800M params, 300ms on T4

takeaways.technique: Benchmark suite for transfer to diverse downstream tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They built RF100VL to measure how well foundation models transfer to many diverse downstream detection tasks, instead of trusting a single reference benchmark.
